messages:
maria: FYI canary p95 just jumped from ~110ms -> 380ms after the last micro-optimizer rollout. Dashboard shows correlated increases in kv-cache misses. deploy-bot suggested an autorevert but flagged low confidence :thinking_face:

sam: thanks — which cohort? global or just eu-west?

maria: mostly eu-west and us-west-1, small spike in APAC. traffic slice for canary is 8%.

deploy-bot: ALERT: canary-slo-crossed (p95 > 300ms) · suggestion: autorevert to v2.6.3 (confidence 0.62) · reason: kernel flag + increased kv cache churn

priya: autorevert confidence low, I'd prefer a manual hold so we can gather trace samples and confirm root cause. 

lee-oncall: agree with @priya. Put a manual hold on the rollout now. If we revert immediately we lose traces. Can ops capture a dump?

ops-runner: running capture: `rdwctl dump traces --canary --since 5m --out /tmp/canary-dump.tar.gz` — started. ETA ~90s

sam: tagging customer-impact: none reported so far. CS on standby to draft a proactive note if we escalate.

maria: decision: manual hold, pin route so the rest of rollout pauses. Sam, please pin host group to v2.6.3 for now. 

sam: executing pin: `releases pin --group canary --to v2.6.3 --reason "p95 spike; manual hold"` — done. :white_check_mark:

priya: adding rollback criteria for go/no-go: 1) p95 returns <200ms for 10m with stable kv-cache hitrate OR 2) we observe client errors increase >0.5% -> immediate rollback.

lee-oncall: +1 on criteria. Also add: if trace root cause points to allocator diff, plan for hotpatch revert of allocator flag.

maria: ops dump in S3: s3://rdw-dumps/canary/1713465432-canary-dump.tar.gz. I'm sharing flamegraphs in the analysis channel next.

deploy-bot: NOTE: autorevert suppressed by operator hold. To re-enable autorevert, run: `deploybot enable-autorevert --strategy canary`

sam: preparing customer-facing blurb in #customer-notices: "Small performance regression observed in a canary subset; rollout paused while we investigate. No customer-facing errors at this time. We'll update in 30m." Draft ready, posting after we confirm pin.

priya: ops, if traces show allocator hot path, we'll roll back the kernel flag via: `opsctl patch kernelcfg --unset experimental_alloc_v2` and then restart canary pool. Who owns the restart?

ops-runner: I can coordinate restarts. If we revert the flag I'll roll sequential restarts on the canary nodes with `rolling-restart --group canary --wait 60s`

lee-oncall: timeline check: capture + analysis target 15m. If we don't have a clear fix by then, initiate manual rollback to v2.6.2 for hosted and notify Dedicated customers about a timed maintenance window.

maria: adding release notes note: "Investigating p95 regression observed in canary post-optimizer rollout; pause in rollout. Potential revert planned. Affected: internal canary subset only." Will push to docs.

sam: CS notified and queued a template for customers if we need to announce a maintenance window. Legal ok with template.

priya: if we decide to rollback, runbook: 1) create rollback ticket (#ops-RB-<ts>) 2) pin routes to previous stable 3) run `releases rollback --to v2.6.2 --scope canary,hosted` 4) monitor p95 and error rate for 30m 5) publish postmortem draft.

maria: agreed. For now we hold. If traces point to allocator/kv churn -> execute hotpatch revert first. If not, follow full rollback runbook.

ops-runner: analysis complete — flamegraphs suggest increased mem-copy in kernel allocator path. Uploading short note to thread.

maria: ok hotpatch path then. Priya can you approve hotpatch revert?

priya: approved. Please run `opsctl patch kernelcfg --unset experimental_alloc_v2 --reason "canary perf regression"` and then `rolling-restart --group canary --wait 60s`.

ops-runner: running hotpatch revert now. Command output: ```patch applied: experimental_alloc_v2 unset
restarting node canary-a ... ok
restarting node canary-b ... ok
restarting node canary-c ... ok```

deploy-bot: MONITOR: after hotpatch revert, p95 dropped from 380ms -> 130ms across canary within 3m. Autorevert remains suppressed by operator hold.

sam: excellent. Maria — we should unpin and continue a slow rollout, or keep pin and further observe?

maria: recommend unpin for gradual rollout: increase to 25% over 30m, keep close monitoring and rollback criteria in place. Sam, update rollout plan and release notes to reflect hotpatch revert and resumed gradual rollout.

sam: updating rollout: `releases resume --group canary --to v2.6.4 --increment 5%/5m --max 25%` — done. Posting updated note to #release-log.

priya: leaving hold on autorevert for another 60m to avoid flip-flop. We'll reconvene if metrics wobble.

lee-oncall: acknowledged. I'll stay on standby for the next 60m.

maria: thanks everyone. Postmortem owner assigned: @priya. Draft due EOD. Closing this thread once postmortem is filed."
